chapter: Second interview: bass, Parker and Miles
title: Lester Young in Philadelphia
summary: Young was sensitive and warm and put down only Stan Getz.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Yeah. He just had a recording, I don't know what it's like. What about Lester Young? You knew him somewhat, didn't you?
Yeah, I played opposite him in Philadelphia, so I got to hear him a whole lot.
He seemed to be a very sensitive --
He didn't put nobody down but Stan Getz.
What did he say about Getz?

Oh, this was when he was sick in the hotel, and looked out the window and Stan Getz was pulling away in a Cadillac limousine. He said, there's a guy that's playing and riding around with my money, playing like me.

Say, riding in a limousine tonight, lookit, Mingus. Willy Jones took me to see him. I didn't know him as well as Willy Jones, because I was playing with the opposite in Philadelphia. And -- what was that bar? Big round bar.
Oh, I know what you mean, I can't think of it.
Bar was in the middle of the floor. Well, when you get a chance, (inaudible).
So I didn't get a chance to know him (inaudible). But he was very glad to have me come over, I know that.
